thread.title: After the Bell: As the Dow Drops 300 Points, Finding a Reason to Smile at Facebook’s Drop

author: Ben Levisohn
title: After the Bell: As the Dow Drops 300 Points, Finding a Reason to Smile at Facebook’s Drop
text:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 330 points today, but the real damage was in the Nasdaq thanks to Facebook (FB), which suffered its largest one-day drop since 2014. In today's After the Bell , we...
 •...look at a group of investors thrilled with Facebook's tumble today;
•...take a look at how Barron's stock picks fared;
•...and explain why Exact Science's naming of Harry Connick Jr. as a spokesperson caused its shares to tumble.
A Market So Ugly...
Now that was an ugly day that almost nobody could love. But do you know who did? Those who'd been betting on a FANGs flop.
Yes, the S&P 500 dropped 1.4% to 2712.92, while fell 335.60 points, or 1.3%, to 24,610.91. The Nasdaq Composite slumped 1.8% to 7344.24. For the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 it was the largest drops since Feb. 8, the day the S&P 500 officially entered correction territory. Ouch.
S3 Partners' Ihor Dusaniwsky, however, writes that "FAANG short sellers are smiling today." He notes that short sellers have been increasing their bets against the Facebook (FB), Amazon.com (AMZN), Apple (AAPL), Netflix (NFLX), and Alphabet (GOOGL) this year, despite the fact that they had lost $6.1 billion on the trade this year heading into today. Those short-sellers cut their losses by about 980 million. Unfortunately, they're still down around $5.1 billion. "In the very near term, there will probably more buy to cover activity," Dusaniwsky explains. "But over the long term, continued short selling should keep FAANG stocks as a group to be the most shorted equities in the U.S. market."
But there's another group who appreciated today's selloff: Those looking to buy tech stocks. Rhino Trading's Michael Block, for one, notes that "we’ve seen this movie before. In my alpha capture books, I am spreading purchases in large cap tech and money center banks over the last hour, making my overall exposure neutral money wise."
Anyone else buying?
Barron's Bounce
Every Monday, we check to see if the stocks we mentioned in the weekend's edition of Barron's got a bounce from our articles. Sometimes it's a direct line from out article to a higher stock price, and sometimes we just get lucky, but we do have a way of moving the market.
It was not a good day to look for bouncers given the market's collapse today. Still, two of our bullish picks finished higher: Gap (GPS) rose 1.5% to $32.23 after Barron's Jack Hough praised its fast-growing Old Navy unit. Umicore (UMICY) ADRs closed up .4% to $13.78 after columnist Victor Reklaitis said that it was a cheaper electric car play than Tesla (TSLA).
And talk about getting lucky: Broadcom (AVGO) fell 3.9% after Barron's warned that moving on from its ill-fated Qualcomm (QCOM) deal may not be as easy as some investors hope, but we suspect that was more about the tech selloff today than anything we said.
Others, though, got walloped, despite our positive calls. Allergan (AGN), meanwhile, fell 1.6% to $166.27 to after Barron's Vito J. Racanelli argued that the shares had gotten too cheap , given the pharma giant's promising pipeline. And banks including First Horizon National (FHN) and United Community Banks (UCBI) lost 0.7% and 0.2%, respectively, after Barron's Ben Levisohn argued that they would get a boost from loosening regulations .
See you next week.
Exact Science: It Shoulda Been Oprah
Exact Science (EXAS) slid on Monday, as Harry Connick, Jr. and his wife Jill were named the faces of The New 50 Campaign, a national effort to raise awareness of the importance of colon cancer screening for those 50 and older.
To borrow a hashtag from Kanye West, it’s #NoDisrespecttoHarryConnickJr, but rather disappointment that the company didn’t get someone even bigger. Canaccord’s Mark Massaro writes that investors were hoping for an “Oprah Winfrey” like celebrity, leading to the decline in the shares.
Yet Massaro defends the stock, calling the weakness a buying opportunity, and the choice, writing that given that Harry Connick Jr. lost his mother to cancer and his wife survived her own battle with breast cancer, they’re a wise choice, especially as they resonate well with 50 to 75 year-olds. He has a Buy rating and $55 price target on the stock.
The shares were knocked around earlier this year on news of a potential competitor to its test for colorectal cancer.
Exact Sciences is down 7.8% to $48.46.
